items.title: Eighteen QB cards ship with an empty 15-Second Answer block
items.found_via: AUG-0025, while reading QB5_C_A#q4 to adjudicate the Management of Change occurrence
items.evidence: A sweep of all 86 QB pages finds 18 practice-blocks carrying the 15-Second Answer label with no body: every question in QB5_C_A.html (q1-q10) and every question in QB5_C_B.html (q1-q8). Both files were authored without that block. No other page in the bank has one.
items.candidate_impact: A candidate opening either page sees a labelled 15-Second Answer and nothing beneath it, on all 18 questions. The 60-Second Answer and the body are present and correct, so the cards are usable, but the fastest surface - the one a candidate revises from - is missing.
items.why_not_done_here: A single-card repair was authored during this session and then deliberately REVERTED. Two reasons. First, the repo's own design note is explicit that a batch manifest cannot own a post-release repair, so the fix belongs in a correction record, not in batch G1. Second, and more importantly, fixing 1 of 18 identical defects would leave QB5_C_A internally inconsistent - one question with a 15-second answer and nine without - which reads worse to a candidate than uniform absence. The defect is a file-scoped authoring gap and should be closed as one sized piece of work.
items.size: 18 cards, two files, one correction record.

items.title: Batch G1 independent clean-context review
items.evidence: AUGUST2026_BATCH_G1_REVIEW.json records independence as SAME_CONTEXT_VERIFICATION and says so in its own caveat field. Every load-bearing number, date and citation in the eight cards was re-derived from a primary or official source after authoring, and two claims were corrected as a result - but the authoring and the checking happened in one session and one context.
items.candidate_impact: An error of understanding shared by the authoring pass and the checking pass would survive both. The risk is concentrated in QB9_D#q12, whose Indian shipbuilding figures are the most currency-sensitive content in the batch.
items.why_not_done_here: A genuinely independent review requires a reader who has not seen the authoring reasoning. That was not available in this session.
items.size: One reviewer, four new cards and four enrichment limbs.
items.closure: Closed 2026-08-24. A reviewer with no access to the producing reasoning was given only the card anchors and a rubric and was barred from the adjudication record, the manifests, the review record and the commit history. It found FIVE defects the same-context pass had missed - two authored by this session (the 5-knot launch/recovery conflation, and the Baltic Dry Index composition) and three predating it (stale MARPOL Annex VI Chapter 4 numbering, a revoked VTS resolution, and SOLAS V/19-1 mislabelled as AIS). All fixed, and a second independent pass was run to confirm the fixes. The exposure this item described was real.

All seven carry a structured negative_search and remain GENUINE_NEW_QUESTION. Two further genuine-new asks joined this queue on 2026-08-24 from submission S007: AUG-0065 (which conventions apply to an LPG carrier - the instrument set for a gas ship, where the liability limb is HNS rather than CLC/Fund) and AUG-0068 (which conventions are engaged when a job is assigned to a 2E or 3E). Both carry a structured negative_search. The queue is therefore NINE asks, not seven. Submission S008 added four more on 2026-08-25: AUG-0080 (the margin line - the subdivision datum the bank teaches the consequences of without ever defining), AUG-0084 (may sea or fresh water be pumped overboard directly from a cargo hold), AUG-0086 (a vessel carrying weapons anchored beyond 24 nautical miles - which convention, and who takes action) and AUG-0087 (the OWS is defective two days before arrival - the single first action). The queue is THIRTEEN asks.
items.candidate_impact: Seven questions asked at the August 2026 Kochi sitting have no card. These are current-value questions and should be produced ahead of the historical follow-up backlog.
items.why_not_done_here: Batch G1 produced the four asks from the newer submission plus the three follow-up limbs. AUG-0015 and AUG-0005 additionally need their scope settled before authoring - the brief flags 'RoRo amendments' as too broad without further candidate evidence, and the emergency-towing 'time requirement' limb should not be guessed from the phrase alone.
items.size: Thirteen cards: the batch-1 seven, AUG-0065 and AUG-0068 from S007, and AUG-0080, AUG-0084, AUG-0086 and AUG-0087 from S008.

items.title: One occurrence remains AMBIGUOUS
items.evidence: AUG-0019 'Risk analysis - why and how.' Batch 1 could not settle whether this is a distinct ask or the same ground as the risk assessment card at AUG-0017, and neither later submission touched it. AUG-0035 'Recent bulk carrier accident - causes, location, accident investigation, survivors' rights, with cross questions.' Its investigation limb is already covered by five cards; its 'recent accident' limb names no casualty; and its survivors'-rights limb is a real gap - 0 hits across all 725 - but the candidate recorded only the phrase plus 'lots of cross questions'.
items.why_not_done_here: Held rather than guessed. Turning a vague recollection into a precise regulatory question is the failure mode the intake contract exists to prevent. The survivors'-rights gap is real and worth watching: if a later submission corroborates it, it becomes a strong new card.
items.update_2026_08_24: AUG-0035 is RESOLVED. S005 named the casualty that S004 could only call "a recent bulk carrier accident" - the MV Ocean Winner - so the hold was released on evidence and a card produced. Only AUG-0019 ("Risk analysis - why and how") remains ambiguous. items.title: Eight batch manifests carried a stale examiner-relationship expectation, and every E/F-series guard expired on the first new card
items.evidence: Two independent defects surfaced when batch G1 added four cards. First, eight manifests declared 960 examiner relationships while the corpus has had 958 since commit 9b1a667 - the count moved 960 -> 966 -> 958 through two governed commits (858adf6 and 9b1a667, the Founder adjudication on two examiner attributions) and the manifests were never refreshed. That failure predates this session and was reproducible on origin/main. Second, every E- and F-series validator asserted 'nothing was added since my baseline' against the LIVE corpus, which is true only until the bank next grows.
items.resolution: Both fixed in this session. The eight expectations were refreshed to 958 with an expected_examiner_relationships_note recording the governed commits that moved the number, so a refresh can never look like a quiet rebaseline. The expiring guards were re-expressed through one shared helper, oral_manifest.sibling_owned_cards, so each now asserts the claim it can make forever: nothing was added that nobody authorised.
items.residual: E6 still fails line_endings_homogeneous_per_file on QB4_I.html and QB9_G.html, which report LF while the manifest records CRLF. Neither file was touched by this session and the runner classifies the gate as PRE_EXISTING_BASELINE from origin/main. It is a checkout artefact of .gitattributes normalisation rather than a content defect, and it makes E6's mutation Z4 uncatchable, since a mutation cannot be caught by a check that is already red.

items.title: QB1_G#q32's candidate-facing question text carries a truncated citation
items.evidence: The question text reads 'Empanelment of salvors. ( ms notice 1 of 202)'. 202 is not a year, and "ms notice" is unnormalised where the rest of the bank writes "MS Notice". The string is candidate-visible and is also emitted into the page JSON-LD.
items.why_not_done_here: Correcting candidate-facing question text is a post-release correction needing its own manifest, and the correct Merchant Shipping Notice number must be verified against the DGMA source rather than reconstructed from a truncated string.
items.closure: Closed 2026-08-24. The number was verified, not reconstructed: the DGMA Nautical Wing casualty page records MS Notice No. 01 of 2026, dated 15 January 2026, as the checklist for empanelment and retention of salvors under Section 255 of the Merchant Shipping Act 2025, with applications commencing 01 March 2026, and the notice published on the same official domain carries that number in its title. The missing digit was 6. Corrected on every candidate-visible surface - the q-text, the JSON-LD Question name generated from it, and the QB1_FG cheat sheet cue - and normalised to 'MS Notice'. The generated examiner index, which carried the old string twice, was rebuilt from the live corpus rather than hand-edited. The historical evidence ledgers were deliberately NOT rewritten: source_wording records what the July sources actually said. Governed by correction_corr_g1_006_salvor_citation_20260824_manifest.json; known trap 50.

items.title: QB8_A#q3 ships raw draft artefacts to candidates

items.evidence: Live in the rendered card: literal '[cite: 1]' markers inside the Regulatory References box (four occurrences), a <pre> block duplicating that box in plain ASCII with ==== rules plus a duplicated CE Oral Tip, literal markdown --- separators rendered as paragraphs, the word "arrow" where a glyph belonged, and a stale correction footer reading QB8 Q16 v1.0 inside a card whose own footer reads QB8 Q3.

items.why_not_done_here: A presentation cleanup of a whole card is a separate bounded job with its own correction manifest, and mixing it into a fresh-intake batch is how blast radius grows.
items.closure: Closed 2026-08-24 for QB8_A#q3. Removed four [cite: 1] markers, the ASCII REGULATORY REFERENCE BOX inside a <pre> duplicating the real reg-box, a second copy of the CE Oral Tip, ten literal markdown --- rules rendered as visible paragraphs, and the draft footer reading QB8 Q16 v1.0; the word 'arrow' became the glyph it stood in for. TWO OF THE FOUR cite markers were inside the REAL reg-box rather than the duplicate, so deleting the <pre> block alone would have left them live - recorded as known trap 51 because it is the general shape of a half-finished repair. items.title: node_security_tests is red on origin/main: .gitignore and .vercelignore cannot be reconciled as the test demands
items.found_via: the full Oral release run of 2026-08-24, which stopped at gate 42 of 58
items.evidence: deploy_surface.test.mjs asserts that every .gitignore pattern is carried verbatim into .vercelignore. Five are not: docs/MIW-master-Question-bank/**/*.txt and the matching **/*.xlsx, **/*.docx, **/*.doc and **/*.pdf. They cannot simply be copied across, because tools/security/deploy_set.mjs parses .vercelignore with a matcher that REFUSES ** by design and throws 'uses syntax this matcher does not implement (negation, **, [], or escapes). Extend the matcher deliberately or rewrite the pattern.' Mirroring them verbatim turns a clean assertion failure into a hard parse error that kills every test in the file, which was confirmed by trying it and then reverting. PRE-EXISTING, and not a regression from this session: .gitignore and .vercelignore are byte-identical to origin/main across every commit made here, the only files this session added are two correction manifests under tools/ which never deploys, and the assertion reads nothing but those two files. The two ** blocks were added by 38a546a, the commit that fixed the untracked raw candidate carrier; the single-star siblings were mirrored into .vercelignore and the new ** ones could not be, so the gate has been red since.
items.candidate_impact: None, and this is the reason it can be sized rather than rushed. The carrier is excluded from the deployment anyway: .vercelignore carries a bare 'docs/' line that excludes the whole tree, which validate_oral_intake.py P3 checks independently and which passes. The defect is in pattern-parity bookkeeping between two files, not in what actually ships.
items.why_not_done_here: Three routes exist and each is a deliberate decision the Founder should make, not a repair to slip into an intake session. Extend deploy_set.mjs to implement ** - the error message invites exactly this, and it is a change to security tooling that needs its own review. Rewrite the .gitignore patterns to a form the matcher accepts, which changes what the REPOSITORY ignores and risks re-exposing the carrier that 38a546a was written to hide. Or teach the parity test that a pattern already covered by a broader one - here 'docs/' - needs no verbatim twin, which is the most correct answer and also the one most likely to be a quiet weakening of a security gate if done carelessly. Nothing here was weakened to get a green: the release is reported as BLOCKED.
items.size: One decision, then a small change to whichever of the three routes is chosen, plus a control proving the carrier stays deployment-excluded either way.
items.closure: Closed 2026-08-25. Root cause was a category error rather than a missing line: the parity assertion compared two files as STRINGS while they are read by two different pattern engines -- git's full gitignore grammar on one side, and the deliberately-restricted matcher in tools/security/deploy_set.mjs on the other, which refuses ** by design. From 38a546a onward the two could no longer express the same patterns, so the string proxy became unsatisfiable while the property it stood for stayed intact. Route chosen: the third of the three the item names -- teach the parity check what it was actually standing in for -- and it was NOT done by blessing five filenames. The check is now two rules. RULE 1, unchanged and still the default: a .gitignore pattern is carried verbatim into .vercelignore. RULE 2, an exemption earned per pattern and never granted by name: a pattern may be absent verbatim only if a broader .vercelignore line already excludes every concrete path it describes, established by expanding the pattern into representative files at three nesting depths (none, one, two) and matching each against the live deployment patterns. Rule 2 is STRICTLY STRONGER than the string comparison it replaces: a string check cannot distinguish a covering pattern from an inert one, which is the exact failure mode the suite's own `~$*` mutation control was written for. Neither .gitignore nor .vercelignore changed a single active pattern -- 41 and 51 respectively, before and after; only their headers were corrected, because both claimed a verbatim mirror that is no longer true. deploy_set.mjs was not touched, so the shared matcher that link_integrity.test.mjs also depends on is unchanged. Teeth, proven by mutation with byte-identical restore and zero residue: removing the broad `docs/` line, removing the top-level .xlsx exclusion, and removing every docs/ line each fail the new rule-2 gate AND the two new nested sentinels (docs/MIW-master-Question-bank/august-2026-intake/S009_raw_report.txt and its .docx sibling one directory deeper), which were added because the top-level sentinel could not see the subfolder exposure that 38a546a existed to close. A fabricated positive control shows an unmirrored pattern with no broader cover is still reported. One mutation is caught but NOT cleanly: inserting a ** pattern into .vercelignore throws during module load of deploy_set.mjs, killing the file rather than failing one test. The diagnostic names the file and the offending pattern exactly, so it is caught loudly; making it a per-test failure would mean deferring PATTERNS construction inside a module a second suite imports, which is a wider change to security tooling than this bounded repair authorises. Recorded as residual, not as a pass. Suite: 613 tests / 1 fail before, 619 tests / 0 fail after. Gate 42 node_security_tests PASS.
items.residual: An unsupported ** pattern written into .vercelignore is caught as a module-load error with a precise diagnostic, not as a single clean test failure. Fixing that means making PATTERNS lazy in deploy_set.mjs, which link_integrity.test.mjs also imports.

items.title: QB2_F#q3 credits the ro-ro fire-safety amendments to the wrong resolution, and the bank contradicts itself about it
items.found_via: AUG-0015, during the live-corpus reuse search for batch G3
items.evidence: QB2_F#q3 is titled 'What are the latest SOLAS Chapter II amendments and their key changes?' Its 15-Second Answer reads: 'SOLAS Chapter II-2 amendments effective 1 Jan 2026 (Res. MSC.532(107)) prohibit PFOS-containing fire-extinguishing media above 10 mg/kg, alongside enhanced Ro-Ro detection and cargo control room alarm requirements.' The PFOS half is correct. The ro-ro half is not: MSC.532(107) is the PFOS / lifting appliances and anchor handling winches / electronic inclinometers / Polar Code package. The vehicle, special category and ro-ro space fire-safety amendments to SOLAS II-2/20 are Res. MSC.550(108), with the companion FSS Code amendments in Res. MSC.555(108). The body of the same card repeats the error under 'Ro-Ro/vehicle space detection'. QB10_B#q1 states the same package CORRECTLY under MSC.550(108) and MSC.555(108), so two paid cards in the bank now disagree with each other about which resolution carries the requirement.
items.candidate_impact: This is the exact failure the bank's own known-traps list calls the wrong-regulation-number class, and it is live on a paid page. A candidate who memorises QB2_F#q3 will quote MSC.532(107) for a ro-ro fire question and be corrected by the examiner - and the bank's own CE Oral Tip on QB10_B#q1 says Nair asks for the resolution number verbatim. It is worse than a silent gap, because the card reads authoritative.
items.why_not_done_here: Correcting candidate-facing regulatory content on an already-published card is a post-release correction and needs its own correction manifest, its own digest pin and its own review - the OPEN-G1-006 and OPEN-G1-007 shape. Batch G3's authorisation covers the thirteen adjudicated August asks; it does not authorise rewriting a card that no August occurrence targeted. Folding a correction into a production batch is how blast radius grows, and it would also put the fix outside the correction gates that exist to verify exactly this kind of change. The AUG-0015 enrichment on the same card is a separate, additive limb and does not depend on the correction landing first.
items.verified: MSC.550(108) confirmed as the SOLAS II-2/20 amendment for vehicle, special category and open and closed ro-ro spaces, plus new weather-deck requirements; in force 1 January 2026; applying to cargo ships and ro-ro passenger ships constructed on or after that date; with retroactive requirements on existing passenger ships to be confirmed no later than the first survey on or after 1 January 2028. FSS Code amendments in MSC.555(108).
items.size: One card, two surfaces (15-second block and body), one correction record with a digest pin.

items.title: The question-bank page search cannot see any answer text, on 85 of 88 QB pages
items.found_via: AUG-0003, while deciding whether an enrichment to QB8_A#q7 would actually make the answer reachable
items.evidence: Every QB page's applyFilters() matches the search box against `c.innerText` of each .q-card. But the stylesheet sets `.q-answer { display: none }` and only `.q-card.open .q-answer` is shown - so on a CLOSED card innerText returns the question text and tags ONLY. innerText, unlike textContent, excludes content that is not rendered. Measured across the bank on 2026-08-25: 88 QB pages carry a search box, 86 search on innerText, 85 also hide .q-answer by default, and those 85 are therefore searching question text alone. The effect is invisible in testing because searching for a word that appears in a question returns exactly what a user expects.
items.candidate_impact: A candidate searching a paid page for a term that is thoroughly answered inside a card gets 'No questions match your search/filter.' QB8_A#q7 is the worked example: it answers the secondary means of venting in full, under the correct regulation, and a search for 'secondary means of venting' on that page returns nothing, because the phrase lives in the hidden answer body. The candidate concludes the bank does not cover it. This also silently penalises exactly the cards that are most thorough.
items.why_not_done_here: It is a one-line behavioural change to a script that is duplicated across 85 paid pages, and the obvious fix - matching on textContent instead of innerText - changes search results everywhere at once and needs its own before/after evidence, not a batch manifest that authorises thirteen August asks. It also deserves a decision rather than a patch: matching hidden answer text will surface cards on incidental words, so the better fix may be an explicit per-card search index rather than raw text.
items.size: One decision, then one script change replicated across 85 pages, with a search-result diff as evidence.
